clue.text: One way to take a border-line view.

definitions.text: One way to take a border-line view.

parts.words: One way to take a border-line view.
parts.note: a border-line view sounds like the view along a frontier, but it is an undecided opinion, taken by perching on the boundary between two gardens

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the country from right on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to commit to either side is literally perching on the divide between two plots.

clue.text: Got in the other way. It's valuable

indicators.note: the other way tells us to put the two clue words in the opposite order, so the second one comes first

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked into a place by a back route and found treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got in' read 'the other way' round, word by word, becomes 'in got'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of gold or silver is a precious object, worth a great deal.

clue.text: Anyhow they can provide the best coals.

definitions.text: Anyhow they can provide the best coals.

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old order, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coal merchant claims to deliver top-grade fuel by any route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' rearranges BEST COALS; the whole clue then wryly says hindrances are what you get from a careless arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurdles and barriers are things in the way, which a jumbled heap of fuel could well become.

clue.text: Dance? O.K., all three.

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in tripping the light fantastic
let's is an eager agreement, a way of saying yes to a suggestion

explanation.surface: A suggestion to dance is accepted by a whole trio at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Three children born at one birth are a set of three together.

clue.text: 4 dn, squared — what a litter

parts.note: three times three gives nine, so a litter born as triplets squared would be a brood of nine

explanation.surface: An animal produces an astonishing brood of three times three.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names any group or set of nine, from the Greek for nine.

clue.text: First step, perhaps: to, getting party off.

definitions.text: First step, perhaps: to, getting party off.

parts.words: First step, perhaps: to, getting party off.
parts.note: getting a party of troops off on a journey starts with loading them into road transport

explanation.surface: A guide to launching a celebration begins with its opening move.
explanation.definitionFit: To board troops onto a motor coach is the military verb for putting them in transport.

clue.text: It isn't, used to, make furniture more mobile.

definitions.text: It isn't, used to, make furniture more mobile.

parts.words: It isn't, used to, make furniture more mobile.
parts.note: small wheels fitted to chair legs share their name with a laxative, which is not what helps a sofa roll

explanation.surface: A remark about lubricating furniture so it moves more easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The purgative made from a bean shares its first word with the little wheels on furniture.

clue.text: The sort of man he'd not miss for reproofs.

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so these letters come in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Telling-offs are described as the kind a certain fellow would never skip.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebukes and scoldings are reprimands delivered to someone at fault.

clue.text: Comprehension: below one's place in society?

parts.note: below means under
standing is a person's rank or status

explanation.surface: A question about whether grasping things puts you low on the social ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping the meaning of something is the same as comprehension.

clue.text: Sydney Smith was convinced it great secret of life.

definitions.text: Sydney Smith was convinced it great secret of life.

parts.words: Sydney Smith was convinced it great secret of life.
parts.note: the clergyman and wit Sydney Smith wrote that the great secret of life lay in a working stomach

explanation.surface: A Victorian wit's view of what really matters for happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney Smith (1771-1845) was an English clergyman famous for his jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Processing food in the stomach and gut was, to this wit, the key to contentment.

clue.text: You can have a bowl when the graduate's in

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate; with the 's it is BA'S, the graduate is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college rule allows a bowl only once the student has qualified.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash-hand bowl or sink is a round open vessel.

clue.text: It's clearly back in the harbour of old

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'It's clearly back in the harbour of old' gives STI from IT'S backwards but nothing supplies O and A; text looks garbled by OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: It's clearly back in the harbour of old

clue.text: Charge, fourteen attractive.

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: the thing that attracts iron

parts.note: a charge is a load, as in a cargo or the powder in a gun
a stone is fourteen pounds in British weight

explanation.surface: A bill for fourteen of something turns out appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetite pulls iron toward it, so the natural magnet is the attracting thing.

clue.text: Discourteous claim to have been brought up.

definitions.text: claim to have been brought up.
definitions.meaning: split as ..., a boast of good upbringing

explanation.surface: Boasting about one's fine upbringing is itself rather rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is the opposite of good manners, yet split in two it boasts of a proper raising.

clue.text: Undoubtedly enough to go right round.

definitions.text: Undoubtedly enough to go right round.

parts.words: Undoubtedly enough to go right round.
parts.note: the length of a boundary is by definition exactly the amount needed to encircle a shape

explanation.surface: Someone is sure there is plenty to share among everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary length of a figure is precisely what it takes to encircle it.

clue.text: Obviously none but the brave.

parts.note: Dryden wrote 'None but the brave deserves the fair'; plainly only valiant people fit the bill

explanation.surface: A line about who deserves the fair, echoing Dryden.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions of courage are by nature brave people.

clue.text: Dine and wine, and likewise amuse.

definitions.meaning: to give guests food and drink as host
to divert or delight an audience

explanation.surface: A host feeds guests and keeps them amused as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosting a meal and diverting an audience are both meanings of the same verb.

clue.text: Flirtatious affair at 4 o'clock?

parts.note: to spoon is old slang for to canoodle, and four o'clock is the hour of the afternoon brew

explanation.surface: A romantic dalliance carried on over afternoon refreshments.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stirring utensil for a cup suggests a spot of cuddling at the afternoon meal.

clue.text: So Sally is returning South to pester us?

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Sally is a pet form of Sarah, so Sally is Sarah

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman coming back south means trouble for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester is to badger or torment repeatedly.

clue.text: Dangerous class of creepers.

parts.note: creepers suggests climbing plants or sneaky people, but here means crawling cold-blooded animals grouped as one zoological class

explanation.surface: A warning about a risky group of climbing plants or sneaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes, lizards and crocodiles form the zoological class of crawling animals.

clue.text: Part of a temple-it's in this he lady tumbled!.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A woman takes a tumble somewhere inside a holy building.
explanation.definitionFit: The innermost sanctuary of an ancient shrine is a section of it.

clue.text: These ladies weren't half wild

parts.note: the Furies were called the Kindly Ones to placate them, though they were anything but gentle; weren't half is British for were very

explanation.surface: A remark that some women were extremely angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weren't half' is British slang for 'were extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek avenging goddesses were given this flattering name meaning the gracious ones.

clue.text: Wandering? Yes or no, quite insane.

parts.note: taken as written, chosen from yes or no
mad means insane

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person is roaming in mind, and gets a vague answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover with no fixed home is a wanderer.

clue.text: Fanatical conduct of an artist at

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Fanatical conduct of an artist at' is cut short: RA (artist) + BID needs a missing final word such as 'auction' to clue BID.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fanatical conduct of an artist at

clue.text: Little brother upset, that's the fish.

parts.note: BR is a short form of brother
ill means unwell, upset in the stomach

explanation.surface: A young sibling is distressed about something to do with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish related to turbot is caught in European waters.

clue.text: So symbolic this form of motet.

definitions.note: a noun phrase: this thing that is so symbolic

indicators.note: form of means a reshaping, so the letters of the musical word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of church music is praised as deeply symbolic.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem of a clan stands for its spirit, so it is highly emblematic.

clue.text: Short hymn one may find poor art in.

indicators.note: one may find tells us the letters can be found by rearranging the words that follow

explanation.surface: A critic finds clumsy artwork inside a brief sacred song.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief stanza sung in Byzantine services is a short religious song.

clue.text: In an even more than lordly sort 'of

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'In an even more than lordly sort 'of' is cut short: the final word (probably 'way') is missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: In an even more than lordly sort 'of
